The results show that while the success rate remains relatively unchanged in the LogP and DRD2 experiments, it significantly drops to 33.8% when optimizing QED, likely because the QED score is a function of the molecular weight (and thus, it correlates with the number of atoms).
deciding_fact_authors_own_ablation.consequence: insert/delete -- the entire reason GrIDDD was nominated as FRAMEWORK_NEIGHBOR -- is inert on the task nearest COMPOSE's DRD2 objective. griddd_qualification.adapter_complexity: SUBSTANTIAL -- we would have to supply an edit budget, a successor-fiber notion (GrIDDD draws nodes and edges from a factorized mean-field categorical, so there is no enumerable one-step support), a separable frozen reference law (CFG bakes conditioning into the weights), and a checkpoint. That is method invention, not an adapter.
